mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises (UNRATE) and employment (PAYEMS) falls, it indicates a weakening labor market, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a tightening cycle negatively impacts equity valuations, leading to lower S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are high in a tightening cycle but S&P 500 returns rise, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth (INDPRO) signals strong supply chains, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If inflation is high but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) but declining housing starts (HOUST) indicates economic imbalance, potentially leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, positively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If real sales grow but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is falsified.
